### Separate composition review: performance admission held

The independent M7 composition derived from the G3 resolution query, with additional NULL/BINARY preservation and a separate surface query, was not integrated into PR #180. Its complete five-file candidate, static acceptance and subsequent bounded performance counterevidence are preserved at [fixed SQL review checkpoint 80d7979](https://github.com/jyqj/codecortex/tree/80d7979da10ae242ed4706cd04be74c62194261a/artifacts/checkpoints/p8-SQL-exclusion-hold-a217-20261009).

Four constructed Python/SQLite cases retained exact output parity, but SQL execute/fetch elapsed time increased. Sparse and multi-batch cases show that the JSON membership structure may be rebuilt for each statement execution, so reduced returned rows or VM counts alone do not establish faster queries. The probe does not time Rust JSON serialization or measure this PR's exact G4 binary; the surface-query case also lies outside this PR's production scope. It is concrete evidence to resolve before treating this strategy as a performance improvement, alongside this PR's original sparse-exclusion VM counterexample.

PR #188 remains separately reviewable and Draft while its exact-head CI and performance interpretation are resolved. Its source has not been absorbed by the format-only M7F update of #180. No original TODO or original scale result changes.

admission_recommendation: Proceed independently with the exact formatter-only repairs needed by the real failing CI, without SQL source changes or PR188 product parent; retain original failure and the SQL candidate unmodified.

Do not admit this unconditional JSON strategy as a performance optimization based on reduced returned rows or a dense-only VM control. Local wall regression is concrete enough to require design revision/evidence before that claim; it is not a fabricated failure of the original registered whole-build gate.

A future bounded alternative could retain old SQL membership filtering and retrieve sorted keyset pages only when exclusions actually consume the frontier witness; this avoids eagerly materializing unrelated E for sparse results. This is a design possibility, not an implemented or approved patch: preserve same read lease/snapshot, NULL error behavior, BINARY membership versus original ORDER/DISTINCT, global cap+1, all-kind/batch union, and work accounting.

Do not silently add a temporary write table to read_conn or tune an arbitrary threshold to these probes. Any exclusion-set caching/materialization needs an explicit connection lifetime, read-only/concurrency/error and memory contract.

No additional broad sample matrix is required to reach this hold decision. Existing finite negative and source boundary suffice. Exact Rust compilation/tests remain pending and cannot be inferred from Python parity.
measurement_boundary: Exactly four finite scenarios and twenty alternating observations; cached statements warmed once; same in-memory database/schema/indexes for each old/candidate pair.

Wall fields wrap SQLite execute plus full fetch. They exclude JSON serialization, Rust allocation/BTreeSet costs and native filesystem/locking. A separate Python boundary includes the Python set/filter/global-cap emulation; this is not a Rust measurement.
Progress-handler period=1 VM callback counts were measured in a separate pass with wall callback disabled. Counts are Python SQLite VM callbacks, not native Rust StatementStatus.

Exact canonical queried table definitions and all their original indexes are extracted from the recorded schema; only these four tables are materialized; foreign keys remain OFF because parent files are not queried. No writes occur during paired query timing.

The sparse 10000 exclusions are real distinct strings unrelated to returned dependents, a constructed valid membership case. This establishes a possible regression, not its frequency in the original C8 corpus.
All old/candidate results preserve the same global sorted distinct cap output in these cases. This is not a replacement for the broader original semantic tests.

Twenty observations are a bounded local design check, not an N30 registered study or confidence-interval/performance gate. Ratios cannot be applied to original whole-build wall time or the 20% acceptance gate.

static_cost_findings.finding: Borrowing one Rust JSON string removes explicit per-statement Rust clone, but SQLite still receives it for each statement execution. The matching-row NOT IN subquery builds an ephemeral membership index via json_each; EXPLAIN contains Once/OpenEphemeral/VFilter/IdxInsert/VNext. Once applies within that execution, not across cached statement resets.

For B statement executions that reach the exclusion expression and E exclusions, exclusion-list traversal can recur B times (approximately B*E value visits, plus ephemeral index work and parsing). Resolution has per-kind 197-key batches; surface has three table statements per 198-root batch. Completely empty matching statements may skip lazy subquery construction, so this is not claimed as unconditional work for no-hit batches.

Resolution deduplicates exclusions before JSON. Surface serializes its passed slice, but the actual reconcile caller forms that slice from state.completed, a set; the current caller therefore has no duplicate-expansion issue. Public arbitrary duplicate inputs are not asserted to be the original workload.

Changing 198 to 197 (resolution) or 199 to 198 (surface) may add batches at boundaries. The present 400-key/root cases use three batches on both sides, so their large regression is not explained by extra statement count.
The canonical dense 600/580 construction reduces returned rows and VM count yet increased measured query wall here. Thus rows or one positive VmStep assertion cannot establish a speedup.

prior_no_small_fix_boundary_original.conclusion: No already established small semantics-preserving patch resolves the performance HOLD. Stop further design expansion in this review.
observed_facts: JSON already serialized once per call; moving it out of inner loop is not a new fix.
Read pool enforces query_only=ON; a TEMP-table population would cross current read-only boundary.
A MATERIALIZED CTE inside each batch remains statement-local, not call-global.

Consolidating into one SQL statement could reduce repeat membership for multiple batches, but changes batching/error-observation and has not been implemented/reviewed. It also cannot by itself remove the adverse one-statement dense and sparse cases.
